components.title: Modular exponentiation via repeated squaring
components.what: Compute successive squares mod 167: 51²≡96, 51⁴≡31, 51⁸≡126, 51¹⁶≡11, 51³²≡121, 51⁶⁴≡112. Decompose 119=64+32+16+4+2+1, then multiply corresponding powers: 112·121·11·31·96·51 mod 167, reducing stepwise (112·121≡25, 25·11≡108, 108·31≡8, 8·96≡100, 100·51≡90) to get 51¹¹⁹≡90 (mod 167).

log.draft:
To compute $51^{119} \pmod{167}$, we use modular exponentiation via repeated squaring. 

1. Successive squares modulo 167:
- $51^1 \equiv 51$
- $51^2 = 2601 = 15 \times 167 + 96 \equiv 96$
- $51^4 \equiv 96^2 = 9216 = 55 \times 167 + 31 \equiv 31$
- $51^8 \equiv 31^2 = 961 = 5 \times 167 + 126 \equiv 126$
- $51^{16} \equiv 126^2 \equiv (-41)^2 = 1681 = 10 \times 167 + 11 \equiv 11$
- $51^{32} \equiv 11^2 = 121 \equiv 121$
- $51^{64} \equiv 121^2 = (-46)^2 = 2116 = 12 \times 167 + 112 \equiv 112$

2. Binary expansion of the exponent:
$119 = 64 + 32 + 16 + 4 + 2 + 1$

3. Combine the corresponding powers modulo 167:
- $51^{64} \cdot 51^{32} \equiv 112 \times 121 = 13552 = 81 \times 167 + 25 \equiv 25$
- $25 \cdot 51^{16} \equiv 25 \times 11 = 275 = 1 \times 167 + 108 \equiv 108$
- $108 \cdot 51^4 \equiv 108 \times 31 = 3348 = 20 \times 167 + 8 \equiv 8$
- $8 \cdot 51^2 \equiv 8 \times 96 = 768 = 4 \times 167 + 100 \equiv 100$
- $100 \cdot 51^1 \equiv 100 \times 51 = 5100 = 30 \times 167 + 90 \equiv 90$

Thus, $51^{119} \equiv 90 \pmod{167}$.

Verification via Python:
```python
assert pow(51, 119, 167) == 90
```

FINAL: 90
